newsitem.title: INDIA: India's move on castor oil exchange right-trade.
newsitem.headline: India's move on castor oil exchange right-trade.

text.p: India's proposal to set up a global futures exchange for castor oil will help both the trade and farmers, the head of the Bombay Oils and Oilseeds Exchange (BOOE) said on Friday.
BOOE president Navin Shah said the proposal contained in the federal budget for 1997/98 (April/March) would lead to globalisation of India's castor oil trade.
The budget was presented in parliament on Friday evening by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram.
"It's a step in the right direction and will send right signals to the world," Shah said.

India, the world's largest castor oil exporter, accounts for about 80 percent of the world export trade in the commodity. It's annual exports of castor oil average around 200,000 tonnes, valued at around 7.0 billion rupees.
"The move will help the overall trade in castor seed, oil and their economy. It will also benefit the castorseed farmers," Shah said.

The move to set up a global futures exchange in castor oil followed the 1994 recommendations of an official committee which called for allowing futures trading in nine commodities, including castor oil.
India has already set up a global futures exchange for pepper which is to become operative in April this year.
India produces about 800,000 tonnes of castorseed, 700,000 tonnes of it coming from the western state of Gujarat. The remainder comes from the southern state of Andhra Pradesh.
Shah said foreign traders and broking houses could become members of the proposed global exchange and provide much-needed know-how to their Indian counterparts.
"We have some infrastructure already available. The Bombay exchange is ready to offer the necessary infrastructure to the proposed global castor oil exchange," Shah said.
